faqs.question: What is the Photoreactor XL used for?
faqs.answer: It's a large-scale, closed-chamber photoreactor with active heating, built for large-scale production and routine lab tasks requiring combined light and temperature control.

faqs.question: What's the difference between concurrent and heat-only mode?
faqs.answer: Running heat and light together reaches up to 40°C, while heat-only mode without lighting reaches up to 60°C.

faqs.question: How do I set up a multi-stage heating and lighting sequence?
faqs.answer: Use the onboard automation to program each stage, heating, lighting, or both, in order, then save it to recall the exact same sequence on future runs.

faqs.question: How many lamps does the Photoreactor XL hold?
faqs.answer: Up to 20 lamps, inside a 20 x 30 x 15 inch chamber roughly ten times the size of a standard photoreactor.

faqs.question: Can I monitor a run without opening the chamber?
faqs.answer: Yes, a spacious chamber window lets you check progress visually while the door stays closed and the safety interlock stays engaged.

faqs.question: How does the sample carousel work?
faqs.answer: It's removable, making it straightforward to load samples before a run and unload them afterward without extra disassembly.

faqs.question: How is temperature kept even across such a large chamber?
faqs.answer: A forced convection heater circulates heat throughout the chamber volume rather than relying on a single fixed heat source.

faqs.question: What safety features come standard?
faqs.answer: A door safety interlock is standard, stopping operation the moment the chamber is opened.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Photoreactor XL in India?
faqs.answer: Get in touch and Inkarp will put together a quote around your temperature mode and lamp configuration.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Photoreactor XL in India?

paragraphs: Scale changes what a photoreactor needs to do well, and Photoreactor XL is built around that. A chamber roughly ten times the volume of a standard photoreactor holds up to 20 lamps, and a forced convection heater keeps that larger space at a consistent temperature rather than letting heat pool unevenly.

Temperature ceiling depends on what else is running. Heat-only mode reaches up to 60°C, useful for straightforward thermal steps. Running heat and light together caps at 40°C, the ceiling that keeps both systems working reliably at once rather than pushing one past what the combined load can sustain.
sections.note: Tell us whether your protocol needs heat and light at the same time or in separate stages, and we'll get you the right temperature mode confirmed.

sections.title: Programmable Automation and Safety Features
sections.tabSummary: Setting sequences and what ships standard
body: Photoreactor XL automation: multi-stage program sequences and standard safety interlock.

A reaction that needs light for twenty minutes, then heat for ten, then both together, shouldn't require standing at the unit managing each transition manually. Photoreactor XL's onboard automation sets and recalls exactly that kind of sequence, so the same multi-stage protocol runs identically every time it's called up.

Safety and usability run alongside that automation rather than working against it. The door safety interlock stops operation the moment the chamber opens, the spacious window lets a run be checked visually without interrupting it, and the removable sample carousel makes loading and unloading between runs straightforward rather than fiddly.

heroParagraphs: Most photoreactors give you light or heat, rarely both working together on a schedule you set once and reuse. Photoreactor XL runs both, and lets you program exactly how they overlap.

Onboard automation sets and recalls program sequences with multiple stages of heating and lighting, so a reaction that needs light first and heat later, or both together, runs the same way every time without you standing over it. Running light and heat concurrently reaches up to 40°C, while heat-only mode pushes to 60°C, a distinction worth knowing before you plan your protocol.

The chamber holds up to 20 lamps inside a 20 x 30 x 15 inch space, roughly ten times the volume of a standard photoreactor chamber, with a forced convection heater, a removable sample carousel, a spacious viewing window, and a door safety interlock standard.
